newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea 3-yr bond yields end flat after early drop.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea 3-yr bond yields end flat after early drop.

text.p: Yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds closed flat on Monday as early drops in yields were offset by late selling sparked by a squeeze in short-term liquidity, dealers said.
They attributed the squeeze in short-term liquidity to the central Bank of Korea's absorption of 966 billion won from the banking system.
The Bank of Korea said it absorbed the cash through sales of five-day repurchase agreements to commercial banks.
The tightened liquidity pushed overnight call rates up by 25 basis points to an average of 14.06 percent.
"A surprise increase of the call rates caused institutions to take to the sidelines throughout the afternoon," said Lee Chang-woo of Samsung Securities.
"I think the three-year yields would move sideways at around 12.50 percent for the time being because the overnight call rate is not likely to set down quickly," he said.
Dealers said trading sentiment was also affected by talks that the central bank was planning to mop up more cash from the banking system in the near future.
Bank of Korea officials were not available for comment.
